  WHY: The premature substitution boundary can misroute a permission-prompt report to an unrelated family; all reporting reviewers rated this NIT, with no severity disagreement.

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py:335-357 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_substitution_end` tracks parentheses but does not skip shell comments (`#`). An unquoted `)` inside a `#` comment within a `$(...)` is treated as the closing parenthesis of the substitution, terminating it early.
  WHY: After the early termination, `command_family` receives a broken token stream and selects the wrong family command (`printf` instead of `git status`).
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  PROBLEM: `_substitution_end` treats a closing parenthesis inside a shell comment as the end of a command substitution.
  WHY: The parser collapses the substitution at that comment character, then selects `printf` as the family command instead of `git status`. That misroutes the permission-prompt report to the wrong family.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py (and twin .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py):335-357 | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `_substitution_end` does not recognize `#` as starting a shell comment, so a closing parenthesis inside a comment is treated as the end of the command substitution.
  WHY: A valid multiline Bash command with a parenthesis in a comment within a command substitution is collapsed at the wrong position, causing the family parser to select the wrong command word. The permission report is then attached to an unrelated family issue or filed as a new issue instead of being grouped with the correct family.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
